title.narrative: Niger, Improving Women's and Girls Access to Improved Health and Nutrition Services in the Priority Areas Project – LAFIA-IYALI

description.narrative: Increase the utilization of a quality RMNCAH-N package of services and improve key behaviors in targeted areas

The development objective of the Improving Women's and Girls Access to Improved Health and Nutrition Services in the Priority Areas Project for Niger is to increase the utilization of a quality reproductive, maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health and nutrition (RMNCAH-N) package of services and improve key behaviors in targeted areas. The project comprises of four components. The first component, increase coverage, utilization, and quality of integrated RMNCAH-N package aims to improve the coverage and quality of services, as well as the continuity of RMNCAH-N services to address under-five mortality as well as maternal mortality and sexual and reproductive health. It consists of following sub-components: (i) increase coverage by establishing and scaling up the delivery of an integrated community RMNCAH-N package; and (ii) improve quality of service supply and remove financial barriers for primary health care. The second component, support demand for health and nutrition services aim to remove behavioral barriers to utilize the RMNCAH-N package and promote key behaviors for increased demand. It consists of following sub-components: (i) social and behavior change communication activities; (ii) primary and secondary school-health and nutrition package; and (iii) improve results achievement by developing collaboration and accountability. The third component, strengthen project management and institutional capacity consists of following sub-components: (i) learning agenda and innovation; (ii) governance, multisectoral coordination, and management; and (iii) project management. The fourth component is contingent emergency response component (CERC).

condition.narrative: Per ESCP the regular E&S monitoring reports providing updates on the environmental, social, health and safety (ESHS) performance ofthe project shall be prepared and transmitted on a three-month basis starting from project effectiveness.

The PIU shall, not later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, (i) recruit and thereafter retain at all times duringProject implementation, the following staff, each with terms of reference, qualifications and experience satisfactory to theAssociation: (A) a Project coordinator; (B) a financial management specialist; (C) a procurement specialist; (D) an environmentalsafeguards specialist; (E) a social safeguards specialist; (F) a gender-based violence expert; (G) a senior accountant; and (H) aninternal auditor; and (ii) acquire a computerized accounting information system for the management of the Project, withspecifications acceptable to the Association.

The PIU shall, not later than one (1) month after the effective date acquire a computerized accounting information system for themanagement of the project, with specifications acceptable to the World Bank.

The PIU shall, not later than six (6) months after the Effective Date, recruit and retain at all times during Projectimplementation, the following staff, each with terms of reference, qualifications and experience satisfactory to the Association:(i) an external auditor, and (ii) two regional accounting assistants.

The Recipient shall furnish the annual work plan and budget for the first year of project implementation, and the evidence whichmay be required for the implementation of the activities included in the draft annual work plan and budget for such period whichshall be furnished no later than one (1) month after the effective date.

The Recipient shall not later than four (4) months after the Effective Date, recruit one or more Service Provider(s) and enter intoa Service Agreement (“Service Agreement”) with the Service Provider(s), whose form and substance shall be satisfactory to theAssociation and in accordance with the Procurement Regulations.
The Recipient shall not later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, prepare and adopt a security action plan, in a manneracceptable to the Association.

The Recipient shall, not later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, select and engage in accordance with the ProcurementRegulations and under terms of reference satisfactory to the Association, and thereafter retain during an agreed period, theservices of one or more Procurement Agent(s), to assist the PIU with selected procurement contracts of the Project, all inaccordance with the provisions of the PIM.

The Recipient shall, not later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, establish and thereafter maintain two (2) regionalbranches of the PIUs (“Regional Branches”), under terms of reference, composition and mandate satisfactory to the Association asfurther elaborated in the Project Implementation Manual and which shall be responsible for supporting the technical implementationof Project activities at the regional level in the Target Regions and for leading dialogues with local stakeholders.
